name: What does a realistic preconstruction phase look like for design-build?

mainEntity.name: How much planning happens before construction starts, and what should owners expect during preconstruction?
mainEntity.text: How much planning happens before construction starts, and what should owners expect during preconstruction?

acceptedAnswer.text: Preconstruction is where most of the project risk gets reduced. During this phase, the team reviews the site, develops the design, refines the budget, coordinates engineering if needed, and prepares permit documents. For luxury projects, it may also include finish selection, long-lead item planning, and construction phasing. The goal is to make as many decisions as possible before field work begins. In Los Angeles, this stage can take longer because of plan check, structural coordination, and neighborhood-specific requirements. Homeowners should expect meetings, revisions, and budget updates before any major construction starts. A rushed preconstruction phase usually leads to more problems later. The best firms treat this stage as part of the service, not as a delay.
acceptedAnswer.description: Preconstruction usually includes site review, design development, budgeting, permitting strategy, engineering coordination, and material planning. This phase can take weeks or months depending on project complexity. A strong preconstruction process reduces construction surprises and improves schedule accuracy.
